subject: Tenant insight ingest + exception playbook for sharp Acme cost spike
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-08-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Tenant insight ingest + exception playbook for sharp Acme cost spike

Team —

Quick context: Acme flagged a ~4x increase in per-request cost for their top route ("/generate/retail-recs") yesterday. They shared the CSV attached with per-request attributes; looks like a combination of long sequences from a small subset of tenants + repeated retries caused by a downstream timeout. They are asking for a confident root cause and an immediate mitigation we can surface via Console.

Asks:
- Short-term: provide a console view (or ad-hoc report) that shows per-tenant cost breakdown for the last 72h, with P50/P95/P99 latency and total token cost per tenant. We need to identify the top 10 tenants driving cost.
- Medium-term: instrument an ingest pipeline that stores an indexed tenant_id + route + model_variant + token_count + latency + exception_type for sampled requests for 7d.
- Operational: draft a playbook for alerting + automated sampling when tenant cost per hour > $X threshold or route-level P99 > 3s, including steps for canary routing to cheaper model variants.

Attached: sample slice from Acme (acme-cost-sample-20260803.csv).

Priority: this is an enterprise escalation — let's treat it P1 for observability and immediate Console surface.

Next steps I propose: Jonas to propose ingestion schema and storage estimate; Marcus to flag any runtime perf implications; Evelyn to scope the Console UX changes and a rollout plan; Laura to coordinate comms to Acme so they have visibility.

Thanks —
Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Mobile: +1-415-555-0123
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-04T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant insight ingest + exception playbook for sharp Acme cost spike

Thanks for the context, Olga. I pulled the sample and had a couple quick clarifying questions before we design ingestion:

1) Is tenant_id already present consistently in request metadata on the edge? If not we need a short SDK/edge change for guaranteed propagation (can be a header or token).
2) Do we need per-token breakdowns or just total token_count per request? Per-token increases storage and query cost significantly.

Preliminary thought: we can add a lightweight event forwarder that emits a compact JSON per-sampled request into our observability Kafka topic. Minimum fields: tenant_id, route, model_variant, token_count, latency_ms, http_status, exception_class, request_id, timestamp. We should avoid per-token histograms at first.

Constraints: storing 7d of sampled data at 10% sampling for 100k rps is non-trivial; I'll work with Jonas on sizing. If this remains P1, we'll need a short-lived increase to retention or archive to cheaper object storage with an indexed catalog for queries.

I'll block time to sketch the schema today. Marcus
Engineering — Runtime
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-05T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant insight ingest + exception playbook for sharp Acme cost spike

Agree with Marcus. A couple product items to add:

- Console UX: a temporary "tenant-cost" explorer that shows top tenants by total cost, count, average token_count, and P99 latency. Include an export button so AMs can pull CSVs for customers.
- Alerts: default thresholds (tweakable by tier) — tenant_hourly_cost > $5000 for enterprise; route_P99 > 3s; repeated 5xx rate > 1% over 15m.
- Rollout: start with a private beta for our top 10 enterprise customers (including Acme), with a canary that exposes only their data.

I've created SUP-4621 and added initial acceptance criteria and UX mockups (link in thread). Marcus/Jonas — can you add tech acceptance criteria and a rough ETA so I can brief CS and AMs?

Evelyn
Product Manager — Console & Observability
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-05T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant insight ingest + exception playbook for sharp Acme cost spike

Plan sketch (high level):

1) Instrumentation — create an event schema as Marcus suggested and add a lightweight sampler at the gateway with configurable rate per tenant (default 1%). For Acme we can bump to 10% during the incident window.

2) Ingest pipeline — events go to observability topic -> stream processor that writes to two stores: (a) a hot OLAP store for 7d of indexed queries (tenant_id, route, time_bucket) and (b) cold object store (Parquet) for 30d archive.

3) Console surface — new backend endpoints that aggregate by tenant and route and power the UI. We will expose top-N queries and histogram buckets for latency.

4) Alerting + playbook — draft attached (tenant-cost-playbook.md) with runbook steps: escalation path, temporary throttles, model variant fallback, communication templates for AMs.

Estimate / impact: initial prototype (schema + sampler + 7d hot store) -> 3 sprints (6 weeks) with 2 engineers + 1 data infra. Additional storage cost estimated ~$2,500/month for our test tenancy at the proposed sampling. We can reduce cost via adaptive sampling.

Requesting: approval to create SUP-4621 epic and allocate 2 infra tickets. Also need AMs to confirm threshold dollar amounts per region/tier.

-Jonas
Observability Engineering Lead
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-06T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant insight ingest + exception playbook for sharp Acme cost spike

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail I wanted. Quick confirmation of owners and next steps:

- Jonas: create the SUP-4621 epic and add the ingestion + storage tickets. Owner: Jonas.
- Marcus: prototype gateway sampler + schema; confirm any required edge header changes. Owner: Marcus.
- Evelyn: UX mock -> Console beta and export CSV flow; coordinate AM/CS comms and thresholds. Owner: Evelyn.
- Laura: own the customer comms for Acme (I will loop in their AM) and validate the CSV attachment with the customer. Owner: Laura.

Please mark the epic P1 and let's have a 30-minute sync today at 4pm PT to align on the immediate canary: Acme will get a 10% increased sampling window for 48h. Laura I asked the AM to be on the call.

I'll follow up with an email we can share with Acme to set expectations (draft in the Drive link).

—Olga
